# Gallivant import capabilities (doc/gallivant/caps.md): the compiler
# enforces //caps: directives at module boundaries, using the effective
# capability set each package records in its export data.

[short] skip 'compiles several modules'

# cmd/go passes the module path of the package being compiled to the
# compiler, but not when compiling the standard library.
go build -n -a -o $devnull ./ok
stderr 'compile.* -p main .*-modpath=example\.com/app'
stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .* -std'
! stderr 'compile.* -p fmt .*-modpath'

# A dependency from another module that uses more capabilities than its
# import is granted fails to compile. The diagnostic shows the full
# required set and where each missing capability originates, including
# capabilities inherited transitively from the dependency's own imports.
! go build -o $devnull ./bad
stderr '^(\./)?bad[/\\]main\.go:7:2: import "example\.com/dep" uses capabilities \[file:write, net\] but is only granted \[file:write\]$'
stderr '^\t\[net\] example\.com/dep/dep\.go:6: import "example\.com/dep2"$'
stderr '^\t\[net\] example\.com/dep2/dep2\.go:6: net\.Dial$'
! stderr '^\t\[file:write\]'

# Granting the full set fixes it. Standard-library imports and imports of
# packages in the same module (even ones that read the environment) need
# no grant.
go build -o $devnull ./ok
go vet ./ok

# Unknown capability tokens are rejected.
! go build -o $devnull ./badtoken
stderr '^(\./)?badtoken[/\\]main\.go:7:22: unknown capability token "bogus" in //caps: directive$'

# A //caps: comment that is not trailing an import is an error.
! go build -o $devnull ./misplaced
stderr '^(\./)?misplaced[/\\]main\.go:9:3: misplaced //caps: directive; must be a trailing comment on an import$'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.27

require (
	example.com/dep v0.0.0
	example.com/dep2 v0.0.0
)

replace example.com/dep => ./dep

replace example.com/dep2 => ./dep2
-- internal/helper/helper.go --
package helper

import "os"

func Home() string { return os.Getenv("HOME") }
-- bad/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" //caps:file:write
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- ok/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" //caps:file:write,net
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- badtoken/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/app/internal/helper"
	"example.com/dep" //caps:file:write,net,bogus
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(helper.Home(), dep.Save("x"))
}
-- misplaced/main.go --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/dep" //caps:file:write,net
)

//caps:net
func main() {
	fmt.Println(dep.Save("x"))
}
-- dep/go.mod --
module example.com/dep

go 1.27

require example.com/dep2 v0.0.0

replace example.com/dep2 => ../dep2
-- dep/dep.go --
package dep

import (
	"os"

	"example.com/dep2" //caps:net
)

func Save(s string) error {
	dep2.Ping()
	return os.WriteFile("/tmp/x", []byte(s), 0o644)
}
-- dep2/go.mod --
module example.com/dep2

go 1.27
-- dep2/dep2.go --
package dep2

import "net"

func Ping() {
	c, err := net.Dial("tcp", "localhost:1")
	if err == nil {
		c.Close()
	}
}
